title: Hypertime and the Possibility of Time Travel
description:
Sometimes in theology and science fiction, it's suggested that agential beings might interact with our world from beyond time as we know it. Making sense of this idea is notoriously difficult and often leads to theories that are contradictory, incomplete, or frustratingly opaque. In fact, for many years I argued that time travel is either impossible—or possible, but not really time travel. Recently, I’ve begun to change my mind.

In this talk, I propose that by introducing the concept of hypertime—a time-like dimension that tracks changes in ordinary time—we can develop more satisfying models of time travel, parallel worlds, divine foreknowledge, and other related phenomena. I will also explore how this framework might intersect with quantum mechanics, simulation theory and metaphysical idealism.

MASSIVE SPOILERS for Terminator (1984) and Back to the Future (1985), but no prior knowledge of these films is required.
